result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers advise against loading on every keystroke and against using both loaders, and both suggest a delay threshold with a minimum display time. B handles the slow case better: it keeps the previous results visible and puts a small spinner beside the list rather than replacing it, which avoids layout shift. B also covers the no-results and error states as well as screen-reader announcements. A's choice of skeleton rows sits uneasily with keeping the previous results on screen, and A leaves out the no-results state. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the right call: no loader on fast lookups, one delayed indicator, a minimum display time, and not adding both. A handles the slow case more consistently. It keeps the previous results visible and puts a small spinner at the edge, which avoids layout shift, and it covers both the no-results and error states. B's delayed skeleton conflicts with its own advice to keep previous results visible, and it can cause layout shift when the number of results differs. B also doesn't cover the no-results state, though it does add useful debounce advice.
